teaser.text: Shopify is the technology company behind a merchant’s shop, not the merchant that owns the goods. It sells the software, payment tools and related services that help a business open a store, take an order and get paid.

stock.title: Shopify stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Shopify's weighted forecast reaches C$281.63 in October 2029, with bear, base and bull scenarios shaped by cash flow, margins, share count and valuation.
stock.opening: Shopify's weighted forecast is C$281.63 in October 2029, a 17% return including dividends, with 25% probability to the bear case, 55% to base and 20% to bull. It hinges on free cash flow after stock pay, share count, net cash and the valuation multiple.
stock.closing: The full Shopify memo also answers how Shopify works, who its rivals are, how management allocates capital, and what risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: Where could Shopify's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is C$249.00 in October 2027, a 4% return including dividends. It is C$281.63 in October 2029, a 17% return including dividends. The forecast assigns 25% probability to the bear case, 55% to base and 20% to bull.
The bear endpoint is 80.06. The bull endpoint is 561.92, versus today's 239.71. The table shows why the weighted result should not be mistaken for the most likely single price.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Shopify, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case begins at 1,485 and ends at 2,000 because weaker merchants, payment costs and credit losses hold margins between 9% and 10%. The bull case begins at 2,730 and ends at 5,120 because international, B2B, offline and AI channels lift revenue and operating leverage. Q2 produced 654 of free cash flow, including 526 after stock pay. Q3 guidance still called for low-thirties revenue growth, but payments usually carry lower margins than subscriptions.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Shopify really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation is the main owner-focused adjustment. Shopify adds it back to operating cash flow because no cash leaves when the award is recorded. Employees eventually receive shares, however, which increases the claims on the company. Deducting stock pay from free cash flow is therefore useful analysis, though it is not Shopify’s own definition.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for Shopify?

paragraphs.text: Shopify’s Class A share is a claim on a fast-growing commerce platform, but its price leaves little room for disappointment. The central question is not whether Shopify is a good business, but how much future cash and control an investor is already paying for.

blocks.heading: What has Shopify guided for the next quarter?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast puts SHOP.TO at C$281.63 in October 2029, a 17% return including dividends, if Shopify sustains cash growth while margins and its valuation multiple evolve as modeled. Management guides to revenue growth in the low thirties and gross-profit-dollar growth in the mid-to-high twenties for the quarter ending September 2026. It guides operating expenses to 33.0%–34.0% of revenue and stock-based compensation to US$150 million.

blocks.heading: Has Shopify kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management has also shown evidence of delivery. In May 2026, it forecast second-quarter revenue growth in the high twenties and a free-cash-flow margin in the mid-teens. The quarter delivered 34% growth and an 18% margin. The lasting test is performance per share, because growth that requires too many new claims can still leave existing owners with too little.

blocks.heading: How have Shopify's revenue and profit trended over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Quarterly comparisons need context. December is holiday-heavy, so its performance is not a fair standard for every later quarter. The more useful pattern across the last eight quarters is continued revenue growth alongside positive operating income.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Shopify's next results?

paragraphs.text: Shopify has scheduled its Q3 2026 results for November 3, 2026, before markets open, followed by an 8:30 a.m. Eastern conference call. Investors should first ask whether revenue and gross profit grew as guided and whether operating expenses stayed within the promised share of revenue.

The quality of that growth matters too. Sales accompanied by sharply higher financing needs or unusually heavy spending would mean something different from growth that replenishes cash. Management’s comments about preparing merchants for holiday demand should show whether discipline is holding.
